document.heading: The Executive Succession and Signature Authority Act of 2025

history.narrative: Resolution KL-CY-2025-029: Posted on the Kiowa Tribe Website: May 09, 2025. Read into record by: Cole DeLaune, District 4, at Legislative Regular Session XCVII-(97), May 10, 2025. Legislature Regular Session XCVIII-(98), June 14, 2025. Legislature Regular Session XCIX-(99), July 12, 2025. Legislature Public Hearing XII-(7), August 08, 2025. Legislature Regular Session C-(100), August 09, 2025. Legislative Regular Session CII-(102), October 11, 2025. Legislative Regular Session CIII-(103), November 08, 2025. Legislative Public Hearing XII, December 12, 2025. Legislative Regular Session CIV, December 13, 2025.

recital.text: the Kiowa Tribe is a sovereign nation and has been so since time immemorial; and,
the Tribe exercises full enjoyment of the inherent powers of government, including self-determination and autonomy over internal affairs encompassing Tribe citizens, lands, and resources; and,
on April 17, 2017, qualified voters of the Tribe ratified the Kiowa Constitution as "the supreme law of the land"; and,

same Constitution establishes the structure of the Kiowa Government, including separation of specific powers among four lateral branches as well as the subordinance in the Executive Branch of the Office of the Vice-Chairman, the occupant of which serves at the pleasure of the Chairman of the Tribe; and, ,
the Constitution, in Article XII, Section 9 provides: "Any vacancy in the Office of Vice-Chairman shall be filled by appointment by the Chairman"; and,
the Kiowa Constitution is silent regarding a line of Executive Branch succession beyond the assumption of the Office of Chairman by a Vice-Chairman; and,
the Office of the Vice-Chairman remained vacant for approximately half of one year in 2024 and 2025; and,
prolonged vacancies in the Office of Vice-Chairman introduce the risk of chaos and operational disarray into the Tribe government; and,

the premise that either the authors of or the voters who approved the Constitution intended to court the peril of Tribe operations plunging into dysfunction in the event of concurrent vacancies in the Offices of Chairman and Vice-Chairman defies credulity; and,
on multiple occasions, the Chairman has granted in his absence from the seat of Kiowa government undefined "signature authority" to appointed officials who are not Members of the Tribe; and
the Legislature is vested with the authority to pass laws and resolutions pursuant to Article VI, Section 6(a) of the Constitution of the Kiowa Tribe; and,

the Legislature has determined that statutory codification of a line of succession as well as protocols for the assignment of "signature authority" by the Chairman are necessary in the interests of bolstering protection against the possibility of operational crises;
that the Legislature hereby enacts "The Executive Succession and Signature Authority Act of 2025."

procedural-data.text: The foregoing Resolution KL-CY-2025-029 was duly voted upon by the Legislature on December 13, 2025, at a Legislative Regular Session CIV-(104), with a vote of (4) in favor and (0) opposed, (0) abstaining, and (3) absent, according to the authority vested in the Legislature by the Constitution of the Kiowa Tribe.

text.b: DELIVERY OF THE RESOLUTION AND LAW TO THE CHAIRMAN

procedural-data.text: Resolution No. KL-CY-2025-029 was presented to the Chairman of the Kiowa Tribe on the 19th day of December, 2025, pursuant to the Article VI, Section 8(a)(iv) of the Constitution of the Kiowa Tribe, and will become effective after signature by the Chairman or veto override by the Legislature, and as otherwise required by the Constitution.
[ ] VETO - RETURNED TO LEGISLATURE WITH EXPLANATION:
Presented by the Chairman to the Legislature on the ____ day of _________, 2025.

The foregoing Legislative Order, KLO-CY-2025-00X was duly voted upon by the Legislature on __________________, 2025, at a Legislative Override Order Session with a vote of ______ in favor and _____ opposed, and _____ abstaining, _____Absent. Pursuant to the authority vested in the Legislature by the Constitution of the Kiowa Tribe.

section.text: This enactment shall be cited as "The Executive Succession and Signature Authority Act of 2025."

This enactment shall provide for the performance of the duties of the office of Chairman of the Tribe in the event of removal, resignation, death, or other inability of both the Chairman and Vice Chairman.
To the extent there is a conflict, this Act supersedes and replaces all prior and existing policies, regulations, or rules whether written, verbal, official, or informal.
If for any reason concurrent vacancies occur in the Offices of Chairman and Vice Chairman, and:

para.text: More than six months remain in the term, the Election Commission shall conduct a Special Election to fill the vacancies within forty-five days.

Less than six months remain in the term, then a qualified official of the Executive Branch consistent with the succession provided in this law shall serve as Acting Chairman until the conclusion of the term.

section.text: In the event that a Special Election is conducted by the Election Commission consistent with provisions of this enactment, then the candidates for Chairman and Vice-Chairman with the highest share of the vote shall be sworn into office by a Justice of the Kiowa Supreme Court upon the certification of Election results by the Commission upon the conclusion of the 48hours provided for protests and challenges of results to the Commission.

para.text: If by reason of death, resignation, removal from office, inability, or failure to qualify, there is neither a Chairman nor a Vice Chairman to discharge the powers and duties of the office of Chairman of the Tribe, then the officer of the Tribe who (a) is highest on the following list and (b) who is an enrolled Member of the Tribe and (c) who is not under disability to discharge the powers and duties of the office of Chairman shall act as Chairman until such a time as a Chairman is elected:
Executive Director of the Kiowa Education Agency
Executive Director of Housing and Community Development
Executive Director of Health and Human Services
The person serving as Acting Chairman shall be given the oath of office and shall faithfully perform the duties of the office until a Chairman is elected, at which time they shall vacate the office.
The person acting as Chairman or as Vice Chairman shall receive the pay of the office in which they are acting, effective on the date of their oath.

If assuming a position as set out herein would interfere with important duties of the Tribe, or if there are personal or other reasons, then any person in line of succession to assume the duties of Acting Chairman or Acting Chairman may decline and the next person in succession shall be appointed and shall take the oath of office.

section.text: Assumption of the powers and duties of the Chairman of the Tribe by an individual serving as Acting Chairman consistent with the provisions of this law shall not be held to constitute resignation from the office by virtue of the holding of which they qualify to act as Chairman. Any officer serving as Acting Chairman consistent with the provisions of this enactment shall delegate the powers and duties of their office to a subordinate of their choice within their respective Division until such a time as their service as Acting Chairman concludes. Any designee to whom same powers and duties are delegated shall receive the pay of the office in which they are acting.

If for any reason the Chairman of the Tribe seeks to delegate signature authority in the course of their term of office, the Chairman shall transmit written notice to the Legislature and such authority shall be vested in the officer of the Tribe who (a) is highest on the following list and (b) who is an enrolled Member of the Tribe and (c) who is not under disability to discharge such authority:

para.text: Executive Director of the Kiowa Education Agency
Executive Director of Housing and Community Development
Executive Director of Health and Human Services

section.text: Such authority shall encompass only enforcement of court orders and procedural approval of requisitions, expenses, and procurements internal to the Tribe and consistent with the Annual Budget. No delegation of signature authority shall be construed to constitute power to sign legislation into law or to veto enactments; to negotiate or sign treaties, contracts, compacts, or gaming management contracts; to issue nominations for appointments; or to represent the Tribe in negotiations with other governments.
This Act is effective upon signature of the Chairman of the Kiowa Tribe or upon signature of the Speaker of the Kiowa Legislature following legislative override.
